candidate.question: What value should be used for the convective heat transfer coefficient on the external surface of the heat exchanger shell?
candidate.reason: The external heat transfer coefficient significantly affects the predicted shell temperature distribution. Published correlations give values ranging from 5 to 25 W/m2K depending on assumed wind conditions.

alternatives.label: Low estimate (5 W/m2K)
alternatives.description: Use a conservative low value assuming still air conditions on the external surface.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Conservative for thermal stress analysis (predicts higher shell temperatures). May overestimate thermal gradients and result in oversized thermal protection.

alternatives.label: Nominal estimate (15 W/m2K)
alternatives.description: Use a moderate value based on typical outdoor installation with light wind conditions.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Represents a reasonable expected condition. Neither conservative nor unconservative; may not bound worst-case scenarios.

alternatives.label: High estimate (25 W/m2K)
alternatives.description: Use an optimistic high value assuming forced convection from sustained wind.
alternatives.tradeoffs: Predicts lower shell temperatures. Unconservative for thermal stress if actual wind conditions are calmer than assumed.

candidate.uncertainty: Site-specific wind data is not available. The assumed convection coefficient could vary by a factor of 5 depending on installation conditions.
